text:
The governance session was a negotiation and you navigated it well.

The expansion continues, under modified language and with amended consent protocols and with a recorded acknowledgment of the Commission findings that three senior members abstained from voting on and seven voted to accept. The internal balance has shifted in a way that is not visible from outside the institution but is real and is documented.

You are in a better position now than you were at the start of Chapter 4. You have more influence, more access, more of the internal trust that translates to the ability to push on things. This is not nothing.

You look at the focusing anchor on your desk.

It still hums. It has hummed since the first week of the first chapter, through assessments and the Conclave's interest in you and the month you spent inside the liaison programme. It hums with a frequency you have learned to read as approval — as consonance between what you're doing and what the object was built to want from the person carrying it.

You are not entirely certain the feeling it produces in response is yours.

Chapter 5 will resolve that question one way or another. The anchor will hum or it will stop humming, and you will find out what the silence means, and whether you want to know.

You have been very successful inside a structure whose foundations you have spent four chapters documenting. These are two facts that will need to be the same thing, eventually, or they will need to stop being true simultaneously.
